subject: Urgent: Meridian Commerce — Latency & Error Surge / Follow-up and Assurance
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@meridian.co>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Meridian Ops <ops@meridian.co>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:12:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors / severe checkout latency — urgent

Evelyn —

We started seeing a sharp increase in checkout latency and a growing rate of 5xx errors on our Redwood-backed product recommendation endpoint starting ~13:50 PDT. This hit peak impact around 14:00 where average p95 jumped to ~2.9s and the error rate climbed to ~6% for 10 minutes. That put several live promotions into a degraded state and directly impacted conversion during a critical marketing window.

Our ops team has temporarily diverted traffic and rolled partial traffic to an older inference variant; conversion is still down ~8% during the window. Can you confirm you have a bridge and a timeline for root cause and mitigation? This is high visibility for us — CFO is looped.

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Eng, Meridian Commerce

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@meridian.co>, Meridian Ops <ops@meridian.co>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 15:10:45 -0700
Subject: Bridge notes / initial findings

Team — quick notes from the bridge (summary for the thread):
- Observed: p50/p95 token generation latency increased coincident with a canary kernel rollout at 13:42 PDT.
- Error signal: transient memory pressure on a subset of GPUs triggering OOM-handling in the runtime; that path returns 500 for some mid-sized payloads.
- Hypothesis: a change in the batching heuristic combined with a quantization parameter tweak in the 13:40 deploy caused larger-than-expected batch formation for longer sequences, increasing KV cache churn and memory fragmentation.
- Evidence: heap snapshot and KV cache delta included (initial_heap_profile.png).

Immediate actions taken:
- Canary halted at 13:58 (stop further rollouts)
- Traffic routed to stable variant for affected routes (Meridian Ops coordination)
- Temporary batching throttle applied on the host pool serving their region (reduced p95 from 2.9s to ~680ms for routed traffic)

Next steps (short):
- Rollback the quantization param and revert batching heuristic on the canary cluster for a controlled A/B tomorrow unless QA flags new regressions
- Prepare an RCA packet for Meridian and execs with timeline, root cause, and recovery steps — target delivery EOD tomorrow 6/8

Jonas
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@meridian.co>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Exec summary & approval request for remediation

Evelyn/Jonas — looping execs for approval to proceed with two targeted mitigations we discussed on bridge:
1) Roll back the quantization parameter change in the 13:40 canary (low-risk, requires a short rolling restart of canary nodes).
2) Apply a conservative batching cap (limit max tokens per batch) globally for Meridian traffic until we ship a long-term fix.

Impact & risk: rollback is low risk and expected to restore memory headroom; batching cap will add slight cost but preserves latency SLOs. We should also open a Jira to track the postmortem and follow tasks: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-1289

Please confirm (Kimberly as ENG approval, David as ops/finance sign-off for cost implications). If no objections, implement 09:30–09:45 PDT.

Kimberly Park
VP, Platform Product
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@meridian.co>, Meridian Ops <ops@meridian.co>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Meridian incident — high-level RCA and immediate remediation applied

Alex / Laura —

Thank you again for patience during the bridge. Below is a concise RCA and what we changed today: 

What happened
- A canary deployment that included a heuristics tweak to batching plus a quantization parameter change increased batch sizes for longer sequences. This caused greater KV cache churn and transient memory pressure on a subset of GPU hosts, triggering the runtime OOM path that produced 500 responses for affected requests.

What we did (immediate)
- Halted the canary and routed Meridian traffic to stable variants at 13:58 PDT (you were switched over at ~14:05)
- Applied a conservative batching cap for Meridian traffic (reduced p95 markedly)
- Rolled back the quantization param on the canary cluster (approved and executed at 09:35 PDT on 6/8)

Impact window
- Start: ~13:50 PDT 6/7
- Peak error spike: ~13:58–14:10 PDT
- Mitigation in traffic: ~14:05 PDT

Attachments for your review
- wakeup_rca.pdf — a one-pager timeline, root cause analysis, and evidence (logs + heap snapshots)
- mitigation-runbook.xlsx — step-by-step mitigations we executed and short-term controls we recommend

Planned follow-up
- We propose a short executive readout and Q&A on Wed 6/9 at 16:00 PDT to walk through the RCA packet and permanent remediation timeline. Our team will provide concrete owners, deliverables, and a verification plan.

Commitments (short)
- Deliver permanent batching heuristic fix and regression test by 6/18 (owner: Jonas)
- Add a canary memory-usage guard and alerting rule by 6/14 (owner: SRE team)
- Offer a 30-day observability review for Meridian routes (owner: Evelyn)

Please confirm the 6/9 readout time or suggest an alternative.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: wakeup_rca.pdf, mitigation-runbook.xlsx)

Evelyn Hart
